steps.title: Import fs, path, and process modules
steps.instruction: Import the fs, path, and process modules using require() statements.
steps.hint: Use the require() function to import each module. For example: const fs = require('fs');
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: importing a module
const http = require('http');
steps.seedCode: // Import fs, path, and process modules here
steps.expectedOutcome: The fs, path, and process modules are imported and available for use in your code.
successCriteria: fs, path, and process are imported using require() statements.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the core Node.js modules.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported some modules, but make sure to import all three: fs, path, and process.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're using require() to import fs, path, and process modules.

steps.title: Create main function structure
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'main' that will contain all the lesson code. The function should be empty for now.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function. Make sure to name it exactly 'main'.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a main function defined that you can later fill with code that uses fs, path, and process.
successCriteria: A function named 'main' is created with an empty body.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the main function structure. This will serve as the entry point for your Node.js code.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've created a function named 'main' with an empty body.
steps.feedbackWrong: The main function wasn't created correctly. Check that you've defined a function named 'main' with proper syntax.

steps.title: Use process.argv to access command line arguments
steps.instruction: Inside your main function, add a console.log statement to output the process.argv array.
steps.hint: Use console.log(process.argv) to see all command line arguments passed to your Node.js script.
steps.expectedOutcome: When you run your script with command line arguments, you will see an array containing the node executable path, script path, and any additional arguments you provided.
successCriteria: The main function contains a console.log statement that outputs process.argv.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully logged the command line arguments array. This shows you how Node.js captures arguments passed to your script.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're logging the entire process.argv array inside the main function.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Inside the main function, use console.log(process.argv) to see the command line arguments.

steps.title: Use path.join() to create file paths
steps.instruction: Inside your main function, use path.join() to create a file path by joining the current directory ('.') with a filename 'data.txt' and store it in a variable named filePath.
steps.hint: Call path.join() with two arguments: '.' and 'data.txt', then assign the result to a variable.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating a file path
const filePath = path.join('folder', 'file.txt');
steps.expectedOutcome: A variable named filePath is declared inside main() using path.join() to create a platform-independent path.
successCriteria: The main function contains a filePath variable assigned with path.join('.', 'data.txt').
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully used path.join() to create a file path. This ensures your code works across different operating systems.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using path.join() with two arguments: '.' and 'data.txt', and storing the result in a variable named filePath.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Inside main(), create a variable filePath and assign it the result of path.join('.', 'data.txt').

steps.title: Use fs.readFileSync() to read a file
steps.instruction: Inside your main function, use fs.readFileSync() to read the file at the path you created with path.join(). Wrap the read operation in a try-catch block to handle potential errors.
steps.hint: Use try { const data = fs.readFileSync(filePath, 'utf8'); } catch (error) { console.error('Error reading file:', error.message); }
steps.expectedOutcome: The main function will include a try-catch block that attempts to read a file synchronously using fs.readFileSync() and handles any errors that occur.
successCriteria: The main function contains a try-catch block with fs.readFileSync() called inside the try block and error handling in the catch block.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented synchronous file reading with proper error handling using try-catch.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using fs.readFileSync() inside a try-catch block and handling errors appropriately.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to use fs.readFileSync() to read a file and wrap it in a try-catch block for error handling.

steps.title: Use fs.writeFileSync() to write to a file
steps.instruction: Inside the main function, after reading the file, use fs.writeFileSync() to write the file content to a new file named 'output.txt'.
steps.hint: Call fs.writeFileSync() with the file path 'output.txt' and the data you read from the original file.
steps.expectedOutcome: The main function now includes a call to fs.writeFileSync() that writes the file content to 'output.txt'.
successCriteria: fs.writeFileSync() is called with 'output.txt' and the file data inside the main function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added synchronous file writing to your function.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure fs.writeFileSync() is called with the correct arguments inside main().
steps.feedbackWrong: The step requires using fs.writeFileSync() to write to a file. Check the function call syntax and placement.

steps.title: Use fs.readdirSync() to list directory contents
steps.instruction: Inside your main function, add a call to fs.readdirSync() to read and list the contents of the current directory ('.'), and log the result to the console.
steps.hint: Use fs.readdirSync('.') to get an array of filenames in the current directory, then console.log() that array.
steps.expectedOutcome: The main function now includes a call to fs.readdirSync() that reads the current directory and logs the array of filenames.
successCriteria: fs.readdirSync('.') is called inside main() and its result is logged with console.log().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully used fs.readdirSync() to read the current directory's contents.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling fs.readdirSync('.') and logging the result with console.log().
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't match the expected action. You need to add fs.readdirSync('.') inside main() and log the result.

steps.title: Use path.extname() and path.basename()
steps.instruction: Inside your main function, use path.extname() to get the file extension and path.basename() to get the filename from the filePath you created earlier, then log both results to the console.
steps.hint: Call path.extname(filePath) to get the extension and path.basename(filePath) to get the filename. Use console.log() to display them.
steps.expectedOutcome: The console will display the file extension (e.g., '.txt') and the filename (e.g., 'document.txt') from the file path.
successCriteria: path.extname() and path.basename() are called with the filePath variable, and both results are logged to the console.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully extracted the file extension and filename using path.extname() and path.basename().
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling both path.extname() and path.basename() with the filePath, and logging both results.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to use path.extname() to get the file extension and path.basename() to get the filename from the filePath, then log both.

steps.title: Use process.cwd() and __dirname
steps.instruction: Inside your main function, add console.log statements to compare process.cwd() and __dirname.
steps.hint: Use console.log('cwd:', process.cwd()) and console.log('__dirname:', __dirname) to see the difference between current working directory and module directory.
steps.expectedOutcome: The main function will now log both the current working directory and the module directory when executed.
successCriteria: The main function contains console.log statements for both process.cwd() and __dirname.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added console.log statements to compare the current working directory and module directory. This helps understand the difference between where the script is running vs where the module file is located.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added both console.log statements - one for process.cwd() and one for __dirname.
steps.feedbackWrong: Please add console.log statements inside the main function to display both process.cwd() and __dirname values.

steps.title: Call the main function and handle execution
steps.instruction: Call the main function at the end of your file and wrap it in a try-catch block to handle any errors that might occur during execution.
steps.hint: Add a try-catch block after your main function definition, then call main() inside the try block. In the catch block, log the error to console.error.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your program will execute the main function when run, and any errors will be caught and logged instead of crashing the program.
successCriteria: main() is called inside a try-catch block, with console.error used in the catch block to log errors.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added execution and error handling to your program. Now when you run it, the main function will execute and any errors will be caught and reported.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're calling main() inside a try block and catching any errors in a catch block with console.error.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check your implementation. You need to call the main function and wrap it in a try-catch block to handle potential errors during execution.
